\begin{proposition}\label{prop:bounded-energy-identities}
\Cref{def:model-energy} and
\eqref{eq:energy-cocycle}--\eqref{eq:energy-sandwich} extend to bounded
\(\omega\)-psh functions. They are continuous under decreasing bounded nets.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Let \(\varphi\) be a bounded \(\omega\)-psh function.  By
\Cref{thm:bfj-decreasing-regularization} choose a decreasing net
\(\varphi_\alpha\searrow\varphi\) of \(\omega\)-psh model functions; after
adding constants we may assume \(-M\leq\varphi\leq\varphi_\alpha\leq0\) for
some \(M\), because the net eventually lies below \(\sup\varphi+1\) and one
may replace it by \(\min\{\varphi_\alpha,\sup\varphi+1\}\), still a
decreasing net of model functions by
\Cref{prop:ch20-model-max} and \Cref{prop:ch21-constants}.

\emph{Step 1: existence of the limit.}  Each summand of
\eqref{eq:model-energy} for \(\varphi_\alpha\) is of the form
\(\int h^\alpha\MA_\omega(\varphi_1^\alpha,\ldots,\varphi_n^\alpha)\) with
\(h^\alpha=\varphi_\alpha\searrow\varphi\) and every
\(\varphi_i^\alpha\in\{\varphi_\alpha,0\}\).  By
\eqref{eq:weighted-monotone-ma} each summand converges, so
\(E_\omega(\varphi_\alpha)\) converges; we define \(E_\omega(\varphi)\) to be
the limit and observe that it is given by \eqref{eq:model-energy}, the
integrals now being taken against the bounded mixed products of
\Cref{thm:bounded-ma-extension}.

\emph{Step 2: independence of the net.}  Let \(\varphi_\beta'\searrow\varphi\)
be a second decreasing net of \(\omega\)-psh model functions.  Fix
\(\alpha\) and \(\varepsilon>0\).  The sets
\[
 F_\beta:=\{\varphi_\beta'\geq\varphi_\alpha+\varepsilon\}\subset X^{\An}
\]
are closed, because \(\varphi_\beta'\) is upper semicontinuous and
\(\varphi_\alpha\) is continuous, and they decrease with \(\beta\); their
intersection is contained in
\(\{\varphi\geq\varphi_\alpha+\varepsilon\}=\varnothing\).  Compactness of
\(X^{\An}\) therefore makes one of them empty, that is,
\(\varphi_\beta'\leq\varphi_\alpha+\varepsilon\) for some \(\beta\).
Monotonicity of \(E_\omega\) at model level
(\Cref{cor:energy-monotone-concave}) and
\eqref{eq:bfj-energy-translation} give
\(\lim_{\beta'}E_\omega(\varphi_{\beta'}')\leq
E_\omega(\varphi_\alpha)+\varepsilon V\); taking the limit in \(\alpha\) and
then \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), and repeating with the two nets exchanged,
shows that the two limits agree.

\emph{Step 3: the identities.}  Fix bounded \(\varphi,\psi\) and decreasing
model nets \(\varphi_\alpha\searrow\varphi\),
\(\psi_\beta\searrow\psi\), indexed by the product of the two directed sets.
Every integral occurring in
\eqref{eq:energy-cocycle}--\eqref{eq:energy-sandwich} is again of the form
\(\int h\,\MA_\omega(\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_n)\) with \(h\) a difference of two
members of decreasing bounded nets and each \(\chi_i\) a member of such a
net.  Splitting \(h=\psi_\beta-\varphi_\alpha\) into its two terms and
applying \eqref{eq:weighted-monotone-ma} to each, every such integral
converges to the corresponding integral for \(\varphi,\psi\).  Since the
identities hold along the net, they hold in the limit.  For
\eqref{eq:energy-first-variation} and
\eqref{eq:energy-second-variation}, note that
\(\varphi_{t,\alpha\beta}=\varphi_\alpha+t(\psi_\beta-\varphi_\alpha)\)
decreases to \(\varphi_t\) for each fixed \(t\in[0,1]\), and that
\eqref{eq:ch26-energy-taylor} exhibits both sides as polynomials in \(t\) of
degree at most \(n+1\) whose coefficients converge; convergence of the
coefficients of a polynomial of bounded degree implies convergence of the
derivatives.

\emph{Step 4: decreasing bounded nets.}  If \(\varphi_\gamma\searrow\varphi\)
is a decreasing net of \emph{bounded} \(\omega\)-psh functions with bounded
limit, then choosing model nets below each \(\varphi_\gamma\) and passing to
the diagonal directed set produces a decreasing model net converging to
\(\varphi\); by Step~2 the value of \(E_\omega(\varphi)\) computed from it is
the correct one, and monotonicity gives
\(E_\omega(\varphi_\gamma)\searrow E_\omega(\varphi)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:bounded-energy-identities}
\Cref{def:model-energy} and
\eqref{eq:energy-cocycle}--\eqref{eq:energy-sandwich} extend to bounded
\(\omega\)-psh functions. They are continuous under decreasing bounded nets.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Let \(\varphi\) be a bounded \(\omega\)-psh function.  By
\Cref{thm:bfj-decreasing-regularization} choose a decreasing net
\(\varphi_\alpha\searrow\varphi\) of \(\omega\)-psh model functions.
Every member already satisfies \(\varphi_\alpha\geq\varphi\), so the
bounded limit supplies a common lower bound.  For an upper bound put
\(B=\sup_{X^{\An}}\varphi+1\).  The open sets
\[
 U_\alpha:=\{x\in X^{\An}:\varphi_\alpha(x)<B\}
\]
cover \(X^{\An}\): at each point the net decreases to a value strictly
less than \(B\).  They are open because model functions are continuous.
Compactness of \(X^{\An}\), by \Cref{thm:berk-proper-compact}, gives a
finite subcover \(U_{\alpha_1},\ldots,U_{\alpha_r}\).  Choose
\(\alpha_0\) above these finitely many indices.  Decreasingness then gives
\(\varphi_\alpha<B\) everywhere for every \(\alpha\geq\alpha_0\).
The tail \(\{\alpha:\alpha\geq\alpha_0\}\) is cofinal in the original
directed set, so restriction to it preserves the pointwise limit.  On
this tail there is a finite \(M\) with
\(-M\leq\varphi\leq\varphi_\alpha\leq M\).
Only indices have been discarded: no potential has been clipped or
translated, and all the approximants remain the given psh model functions.

\emph{Step 1: existence of the limit.}  Each summand of
\eqref{eq:model-energy} for \(\varphi_\alpha\) is of the form
\(\int h^\alpha\MA_\omega(\varphi_1^\alpha,\ldots,\varphi_n^\alpha)\) with
\(h^\alpha=\varphi_\alpha\searrow\varphi\) and every
\(\varphi_i^\alpha\in\{\varphi_\alpha,0\}\).  By
\eqref{eq:weighted-monotone-ma} each summand converges, so
\(E_\omega(\varphi_\alpha)\) converges; we define \(E_\omega(\varphi)\) to be
the limit and observe that it is given by \eqref{eq:model-energy}, the
integrals now being taken against the bounded mixed products of
\Cref{thm:bounded-ma-extension}.  In particular, the definition is finite
and agrees with the model energy when \(\varphi\) is a model function.

\emph{Step 2: independence of the net.}  Let \(\varphi_\beta'\searrow\varphi\)
be a second decreasing net of \(\omega\)-psh model functions, restricted
to a uniformly bounded cofinal tail as above.  Fix
\(\alpha\) and \(\varepsilon>0\).  The sets
\[
 F_\beta:=\{\varphi_\beta'\geq\varphi_\alpha+\varepsilon\}\subset X^{\An}
\]
are closed, because both functions are continuous, and decrease with
\(\beta\).  Their intersection is contained in
\(\{\varphi\geq\varphi_\alpha+\varepsilon\}=\varnothing\).
Compactness and directedness therefore make one of them empty, so
\(\varphi_\beta'\leq\varphi_\alpha+\varepsilon\) eventually in \(\beta\).
Monotonicity of \(E_\omega\) at model level
(\Cref{cor:energy-monotone-concave}) and
\eqref{eq:bfj-energy-translation} give
\(\lim_\beta E_\omega(\varphi_\beta')\leq
E_\omega(\varphi_\alpha)+\varepsilon V\).  Taking the limit in \(\alpha\)
and then \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), and repeating with the two nets
exchanged, shows that the limits agree.  The translated function is used
only as a comparison majorant; neither approximating net is translated.

\emph{Step 3: the identities.}  Fix bounded \(\varphi,\psi\) and decreasing
model nets \(\varphi_\alpha\searrow\varphi\),
\(\psi_\beta\searrow\psi\).  Restrict each to a uniformly bounded cofinal
tail and use the product of the two directed sets.  Every integral in
\eqref{eq:energy-cocycle}--\eqref{eq:energy-sandwich} is of the form
\(\int h\,\MA_\omega(\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_n)\), with \(h\) a difference of
two members of decreasing bounded psh nets and each \(\chi_i\) a member
of such a net.  Splitting \(h=\psi_\beta-\varphi_\alpha\) into its two
terms and applying \eqref{eq:weighted-monotone-ma} to each, every such
integral converges to the corresponding integral for \(\varphi,\psi\).
Thus the model identities and inequalities pass to the limit.  For
\eqref{eq:energy-first-variation} and
\eqref{eq:energy-second-variation}, note that
\(\varphi_{t,\alpha\beta}=\varphi_\alpha+t(\psi_\beta-\varphi_\alpha)\)
decreases to \(\varphi_t\) for each fixed \(t\in[0,1]\).  The expansion
\eqref{eq:ch26-energy-taylor} expresses the energy as a polynomial in
\(t\) of degree at most \(n+1\).  Each coefficient is a finite linear
combination of the bounded mixed integrals just treated, so its limit
exists.  Differentiating these finite polynomial expansions therefore
commutes with passage to the limit and proves the two variation formulas.

\emph{Step 4: decreasing bounded nets.}  Let
\(\varphi_\gamma\searrow\varphi\) be a decreasing net of bounded
\(\omega\)-psh functions with bounded limit.  Fix one index \(\gamma_0\).
On its cofinal tail,
\[
 \inf_{X^{\An}}\varphi\leq\varphi\leq\varphi_\gamma
 \leq\varphi_{\gamma_0}\leq\sup_{X^{\An}}\varphi_{\gamma_0},
 \qquad \gamma\geq\gamma_0,
\]
so the entire tail is uniformly bounded.  By Step~1 the bounded energy
formula \eqref{eq:model-energy} already holds for each
\(\varphi_\gamma\) and for \(\varphi\).  Apply
\eqref{eq:weighted-monotone-ma} to each of its summands, with weight
\(h^\gamma=\varphi_\gamma\) and with every measure slot equal to either
\(\varphi_\gamma\) or \(0\).  The resulting limits give
\(E_\omega(\varphi_\gamma)\to E_\omega(\varphi)\).
The bounded energy inequalities from Step~3 imply monotonicity, hence in
fact \(E_\omega(\varphi_\gamma)\searrow E_\omega(\varphi)\).
This uses the bounded Monge--Amp\`ere continuity theorem already established
in \Cref{chap:bfj-ma}, not a new choice or diagonalization of model nets.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:ch30-finite-bounded-projection}
Let \(f:Y\to X\) be finite surjective of degree \(d\) between smooth
projective \(K\)-varieties of dimension \(n\), and let
\(\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_n\) be bounded \(\theta\)-psh functions on
\(X\).  Then \(f^*\varphi_1,\ldots,f^*\varphi_n\) are bounded
\(f^*\theta\)-psh functions on \(Y\) and
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:ch30-bounded-projection}
 f_*\MA_{f^*\theta}(f^*\varphi_1,\ldots,f^*\varphi_n)
 =d\,\MA_\theta(\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_n).
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Boundedness of \(f^*\varphi_i\) is clear, and psh-ness is
\Cref{prop:finite-pullback-psh}.  By
\Cref{thm:bfj-decreasing-regularization} choose, for each \(i\), a
decreasing net \(\varphi_i^\alpha\searrow\varphi_i\) of \(\theta\)-psh model
functions; replacing \(\varphi_i^\alpha\) by
\(\max\{\varphi_i^\alpha,\inf\varphi_i\}\), which is again a \(\theta\)-psh
model function by \Cref{prop:ch20-model-max} and still decreases to
\(\varphi_i\), we may assume the nets uniformly bounded.  Then
\(f^*\varphi_i^\alpha\searrow f^*\varphi_i\) is a decreasing net of bounded
\(f^*\theta\)-psh model functions.

Fix \(h\in C^0(X^{\An})\); we must show that the two sides of
\eqref{eq:ch30-bounded-projection} agree against \(h\).  Since model
functions are uniformly dense in \(C^0(X^{\An})\) and both sides are Radon
measures of the same finite mass by
\Cref{thm:ch24-mass} and
\Cref{lem:ch30-pushforward-basic}\,\cref{itm:ch30-pf:radon}, we may assume
\(h\) is a model function, hence continuous.  Apply
\eqref{eq:weighted-monotone-ma} on \(Y\) with the constant net \(h\circ
f^{\An}\) and the decreasing nets \(f^*\varphi_i^\alpha\), and on \(X\) with
\(h\) and \(\varphi_i^\alpha\).  Set
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mu_\alpha^Y
   &:=\MA_{f^*\theta}(f^*\varphi_1^\alpha,\ldots,
      f^*\varphi_n^\alpha),\\
 \mu^Y
   &:=\MA_{f^*\theta}(f^*\varphi_1,\ldots,f^*\varphi_n),\\
 \mu_\alpha^X
   &:=\MA_\theta(\varphi_1^\alpha,\ldots,\varphi_n^\alpha),\\
 \mu^X
   &:=\MA_\theta(\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_n).
 \end{aligned}
\]
The two weighted convergences are
\[
 \int_{Y^{\An}}(h\circ f^{\An})\,\rd\mu_\alpha^Y
 \longrightarrow
 \int_{Y^{\An}}(h\circ f^{\An})\,\rd\mu^Y,
 \qquad
 \int_{X^{\An}}h\,\rd\mu_\alpha^X
 \longrightarrow
 \int_{X^{\An}}h\,\rd\mu^X.
\]
For every \(\alpha\) the two left-hand sides are related by
\eqref{eq:ch30-finite-test}, that is, the first equals \(d\) times the
second.  Passing to the limit gives the identity against \(h\), and hence
\eqref{eq:ch30-bounded-projection}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Why the test function must be pulled back]
\label{rem:ch30-test-function}
In the proof, \eqref{eq:weighted-monotone-ma} was applied upstairs with the
weight \(h\circ f^{\An}\), which is continuous but is \emph{not} in general
a model function on \(Y\) unless \(h\) is a model function on \(X\).  This
is harmless because \eqref{eq:weighted-monotone-ma} allows an arbitrary
decreasing net of bounded psh weights and, a fortiori, a constant continuous
weight after the usual decomposition of a continuous function as a
difference of two continuous psh functions
(\Cref{lem:ch24-psh-difference}).  It is, however, the reason the argument
tests against model functions downstairs rather than upstairs: the class of
model functions is not stable under pushforward, only under pullback.
\end{remark}

\label{thm:ch30-finite-bounded-projection}
Let \(f:Y\to X\) be finite surjective of degree \(d\) between smooth
projective \(K\)-varieties of dimension \(n\), and let
\(\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_n\) be bounded \(\theta\)-psh functions on
\(X\).  Then \(f^*\varphi_1,\ldots,f^*\varphi_n\) are bounded
\(f^*\theta\)-psh functions on \(Y\) and
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:ch30-bounded-projection}
 f_*\MA_{f^*\theta}(f^*\varphi_1,\ldots,f^*\varphi_n)
 =d\,\MA_\theta(\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_n).
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Boundedness of \(f^*\varphi_i\) is clear, and psh-ness is
\Cref{prop:finite-pullback-psh}.  By
\Cref{thm:bfj-decreasing-regularization}, for each \(i\) choose a
decreasing net \(\varphi_i^{\alpha_i}\searrow\varphi_i\) of
\(\theta\)-psh model functions, indexed by a directed set \(A_i\).
Every approximant already satisfies
\(\varphi_i^{\alpha_i}\geq\varphi_i\geq\inf_{X^{\An}}\varphi_i\).
For the upper bound set \(B_i=\sup_{X^{\An}}\varphi_i+1\).
The open sets \(\{\varphi_i^{\alpha_i}<B_i\}\) cover the compact space
\(X^{\An}\), because the approximants are continuous and decrease
pointwise to \(\varphi_i<B_i\).  Choose a finite subcover and then a
common upper bound \(\alpha_{i,0}\) for its indices.  On the cofinal tail
\(A_i'=\{\alpha_i:\alpha_i\geq\alpha_{i,0}\}\), decreasingness gives
\[
 \inf_{X^{\An}}\varphi_i\leq\varphi_i\leq
 \varphi_i^{\alpha_i}<B_i
 \quad\text{everywhere on }X^{\An}.
\]
Thus each tail is uniformly bounded without any maximum or minimum
operation.  Put \(A=A_1'\times\cdots\times A_n'\), ordered
componentwise, and for \(\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)\) write
\(\varphi_i^\alpha=\varphi_i^{\alpha_i}\).
These are decreasing nets with their original limits.  Since the number
of slots is finite, one bound works for all of them and for their
pullbacks.  By \Cref{lem:ch30-pullback-model-calculus}\,
\cref{itm:ch30-pbm:divisor,itm:ch30-pbm:ddc}, the pullbacks are still
psh model functions and decrease to \(f^*\varphi_i\).

Set
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mu_\alpha^Y
   &:=\MA_{f^*\theta}(f^*\varphi_1^\alpha,\ldots,
      f^*\varphi_n^\alpha),&
 \mu^Y
   &:=\MA_{f^*\theta}(f^*\varphi_1,\ldots,f^*\varphi_n),\\
 \mu_\alpha^X
   &:=\MA_\theta(\varphi_1^\alpha,\ldots,\varphi_n^\alpha),&
 \mu^X
   &:=\MA_\theta(\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_n).
 \end{aligned}
\]
The bounded decreasing-net continuity established in
\Cref{thm:bounded-ma-extension}, in particular Step~6 of its proof,
gives \(\mu_\alpha^X\to\mu^X\) and \(\mu_\alpha^Y\to\mu^Y\) weakly.
The model projection formula \eqref{eq:ch30-finite-test} gives
\(f_*\mu_\alpha^Y=d\mu_\alpha^X\) for every \(\alpha\).
Pushforward is weakly continuous by
\Cref{lem:ch30-pushforward-basic}\,\cref{itm:ch30-pf:weak}.
Explicitly, for every \(h\in C^0(X^{\An})\), the function
\(h\circ f^{\An}\) is continuous on \(Y^{\An}\), and hence
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \int_{Y^{\An}}(h\circ f^{\An})\,\rd\mu^Y
 &=\lim_\alpha\int_{Y^{\An}}(h\circ f^{\An})\,\rd\mu_\alpha^Y\\
 &=d\lim_\alpha\int_{X^{\An}}h\,\rd\mu_\alpha^X
  =d\int_{X^{\An}}h\,\rd\mu^X.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Equality against all continuous test functions proves
\eqref{eq:ch30-bounded-projection}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Why the test function must be pulled back]
\label{rem:ch30-test-function}
Pushforward of a measure is tested against a continuous function \(h\)
downstairs by integrating \(h\circ f^{\An}\) upstairs.  The proof above
uses weak convergence of measures, so neither test function needs to be
psh or a model function.  The weighted statement
\eqref{eq:weighted-monotone-ma} has a narrower direct test class: its
weights are bounded psh functions.  In Step~6 of
\Cref{thm:bounded-ma-extension}, weak convergence is deduced from that
statement by linearity on the span of psh model tests and then uniform
density.  This does not assert that every continuous function is a
difference of two continuous psh functions.  Here we use the resulting
weak convergence, and only measures, not test functions, are pushed
forward.
\end{remark}
